points.description: States that a very low eigenvalue corresponds to a principal axis/eigenvector along which the data has very low variance (little information/spread).
points.partial_credit: Half if only says the component is unimportant or has little information without linking to low variance.

points.description: States that such components/axes are not useful (redundant, possibly correlated with other components/features) and can be discarded in dimensionality reduction.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says they can be discarded/ignored without reason, or only mentions correlation/redundancy without discarding.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas: low eigenvalue means very low variance along that eigenvector, and that axis is redundant/not useful so can be dropped in dimensionality reduction. Give part marks for a vague or half-stated version of either idea. Give nothing for wrong claims, e.g. that low eigenvalues mean high variance or the most important components.
